sentences.text: As per prosecution story, FIR was lodged on 20.08.2023 for commission of offences between 22.09.2022 to 16.08.2023.
Written complaint was filed at Police Station against petitioner Dharmendra Kushwaha.
It was stated that prosecutrix came in contact of accused person in respect of purchase of a plot.
He helped her to get a job in Lakme Academy for Rs.25,000/- per months.
Prosecutrix gave sum of Rs.15,00,000/- to accused for doing business of academy.

He assured her Dharmendra Kushwaha vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113799150/
1 that he will transfer academy in her name.

sentences.text: Later on, he took her to Sahara City in a lonely place on 29.02.2022 and against her wishes committed rape on her.
On protest, he used to threaten the prosecutrix to kill her.
On said complaint, police has registered the offence as alleged in FIR.
She was medically examined and no external or internal injury was found on body of the prosecutrix and no opinion regarding rape was given by Doctor.
Statement of prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C., in which she had made similar statement as given in written complaint.
She stated that she was raped 06-08 times by the petitioner.
It was also alleged that he used to beat her.
Vehicle belonging to petitioner i.e. MP-19- CC-2324 was seized.
Vaginal slide of prosecutrix was prepared and in FSL examination report, no sperms were found on said slide.
Father of prosecutrix was in railway service.
He got retiral money of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:58782 3 MCRC-37529-2024 Rs.15,00,000/-.
Said amount was given by prosecutrix to petitioner for business purpose.
Police has collected the document regarding monetary transaction and transfer of money by phone pay and by cheque.

Business partnership agreement between MEL Training &
Assessment Limited and M/s Kailash Associates Proprietor (Dharmendra Kushwaha) was also seized by police.

Prosecutrix has signed the said business partnership agreement as a witness dated 03.05.2022.
5.
Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submitted that petitioner is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the case.
Prosecutrix was consenting party.
They were known to each other for long time.
There is long delay in lodging of FIR.
Prosecutrix has given money to petitioner for help in business.
There was dispute regarding monetary transaction, therefore, petitioner has been implicated malafidely.
No offence under Sections 376, 376(2)(n), 294, 323, 506 of the IPC is made out against the petitioner.
It is further submitted that no cheating has been committed by the petitioner.
If prosecutrix wants to recover any money from petitioner, she has civil remedy available to her.
FIR has been filed to harass the petitioner.
No offence has been committed by the petitioner and charge-sheet filed against him may be quashed.

6. Learned Government Advocate appearing for the State NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-JBP:58782 4 MCRC-37529-2024 opposed the petition and submitted that prosecutrix has lodged an FIR and has given statement in Court under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C.
She has stated that she has forcibly been raped by the petitioner.
At initial stage, prosecutrix cannot be disbelieved.
Offence of rape is made out against the petitioner.
Prosecutrix has also advanced money to petitioner on false promise and prosecutrix is cheated of an amount of Rs.15,00,000/- by the petitioner.
In these circumstances, petition may be dismissed.

7. Heard the counsel for the parties.
8.
Incident is said to have occurred between 20.09.2022 to 16.08.2023.
Report has been lodged after delay.
It has also been stated in 164 of the Cr.P.C. statement that she has been raped repeatedly 06-08 times.
First incident occurred on 12.09.2022 and thereafter, no report was lodged.
Prosecutrix was again raped by petitioner 06-08 times then also she did not lodge any report.

On going through the details of transaction, it is found that money was transfer on 14.01.2022,
13.02.2022, 17.03.2022, 19.05.2022, 05.06.2022, 17.07.2022, 04.08.2022, 24.08.2022, 12.09.2022,
17.09.2022, 19.05.2023 and money was also transferred by phone pay.

sentences.text: After incident of rape also money was transferred in account of petitioner.
Prosecutrix was in touch with the petitioner as well as with the institution even NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:58782 5 MCRC-37529-2024 after rape is said to have been committed.
Petitioner also transferred money into her account after rape.
Aforesaid transaction shows that prosecutrix has not stopped her relationship with the petitioner after first incident of rape.
Prosecutrix was a witness to business partnership agreement which was entered between petitioner as proprietor of Kailash Associates and MEL Training & Assessment Limited.
There was money transaction between petitioner and the prosecutrix.
She did not lodge FIR against the petitioner immediately after the incident.
There was long delay of about one year in filing of complaint after first incident of rape.
Prosecutrix is major aged 26 years on the date of lodging of FIR.
Medical examination of prosecutrix was also negative.
No external or internal injury was found on the body of prosecutrix.
Only general allegation of threatening was made by her.

9. Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of State of Haryana Vs. Bhajan Lal & Ors. reported in 1992 SCC (SUPP) 1 335, has laid down following guidelines for quashing of FIR, which is quoted as under :-
102.

entities.text: State of Haryana Vs. Bhajan Lal & Ors. reported in 1992 SCC (SUPP) 1 335
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the backdrop of the interpretation of the various relevant provisions of the Code under Chapter XIV and of the principles of law enunciated by this Court in a series of decisions NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:58782 6 MCRC-37529-2024 relating to the exercise of the extraordinary power under Article 226 or the inherent powers under Section 482 of the Code which we have extracted and reproduced above, we give the following categories of cases by way of illustration wherein such power could be exercised either to prevent abuse of the process of any court or otherwise to secure the ends of justice, though it may not be possible to lay down any precise, clearly defined and sufficiently channelised and inflexible guidelines or rigid formulae and to give an exhaustive list of myriad kinds of cases wherein such power should be exercised.

(1) Where the allegations made in the First Information Report or the complaint,
even if they are taken at their face value and accepted in their entirety do not prima facie constitute any offence or make out a case against the accused.

(2) Where the allegations in the First Information Report and other materials, if any,
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:58782 7 MCRC-37529-2024 accompanying the FIR do not disclose a cognizable offence, justifying an investigation by police officers under Section 156(1) of the Code except under an order of a Magistrate within the purview of Section 155(2) of the Code.

(3) Where the uncontroverted allegations made in the FIR or complaint and the evidence collected in support of the same do not disclose the commission of any offence and make out a case against the accused.

(4) Where, the allegations in the FIR do not constitute a cognizable offence but constitute only a non-cognizable offence, no investigation is permitted by a police officer without an order of a Dharmendra Kushwaha vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113799150/
3 Magistrate as contemplated under Section 155(2) of the Code.

entities.text: Dharmendra Kushwaha vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (5) Where the allegations made in the FIR or complaint are so absurd and inherently improbable on the basis of which no prudent person can ever reach a just conclusion that there is sufficient ground for proceeding against NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:58782 8 MCRC-37529-2024 the accused.

(6) Where there is an express legal bar engrafted in any of the provisions of the Code or the concerned Act (under which a criminal proceeding is instituted) to the institution and continuance of the proceedings and/or where there is a specific provision in the Code or the concerned Act,
providing efficacious redress for the grievance of the aggrieved party.
(7) Where a criminal proceeding is manifestly attended with mala fide and/or where the proceeding is maliciously instituted with an ulterior motive for wreaking vengeance on the accused and with a view to spite him due to private and personal grudge.
10. Case of petitioner falls in category-7 of said guidelines.

In case of Gaurav Singh Chadhar Vs.
State of M.P.-2023 SCC OnLine MP 247 , Co-ordinate Bench of this Court has observed as under :-
"The Supreme Court has also observed in number of occasions that if criminal proceeding manifestly with mala fide and instituted maliciously with an ulterior motive for wreaking vengeance and with a view to spite someone due to private and personal grudge NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:58782 9 MCRC-37529-2024 then the same can be quashed and cannot be permitted to continue."

sentences.text: 11. Considering entire facts and circumstances of the case, charge-sheet in respect of Crime No.606/2023 registered at Police Station-Kotwali, District-Satna (MP) for offences punishable under Sections 376, 376(2)(n), 294, 323, 506, 420 of the IPC and subsequent proceedings in respect of ST No.152/2024 pending before Additional Sessions Judge, Satna District-Satna (MP) against petitioner, is quashed.
Quashing of criminal case will not affect the civil liability of petitioner.
12. With aforesaid, petition is disposed off.
